questions.question: Why is register renaming critical for modern superscalar pipelines?

answers.c: It removes name-based hazards and improves parallelism

explanations.c: Correct. Renaming avoids WAR/WAW and improves ILP.

questions.question: What type of hazards does register renaming specifically target?
In the simulation, what does it mean if an architectural register maps to multiple physical registers across instructions?

answers.b: This allows multiple writes to the same register without conflict

explanations.b: Correct. This is how renaming works.

questions.question: What happens if there are no free physical registers during instruction issue?

answers.c: The pipeline stalls until a physical register is freed

explanations.c: Correct. Stall occurs when out of physical registers.

questions.question: After an instruction writes its result, when can its physical register be reclaimed?

answers.b: After commit and once no other instructions depend on it

explanations.b: Correct. Safe to reclaim after commit.

questions.question: What allows two instructions writing to the same architectural register to proceed out of order?

answers.c: Assigning a new physical register to the later instruction

explanations.c: Correct. This is how renaming removes WAW.

questions.question: In a register rename table, what does a mapping like 'R5 → P8' indicate?

answers.c: Physical register P8 holds the most recent value for R5
answers.d: R5 has been renamed to R8

questions.question: A student tries to write back a result, but the simulator blocks it. The rename table shows another instruction maps to the same architectural register. Why is this blocked?

answers.a: A WAW hazard is pending and write-back is unsafe
answers.b: RAW hazard must be resolved first
answers.c: There are no more rename slots

explanations.a: Correct. Only the most recent mapping can be written.

questions.question: What would be the main limitation if register renaming is not used along with scoreboarding?

answers.a: Only floating-point instructions can be executed
answers.b: Only one instruction can be in the pipeline at a time
answers.c: WAR and WAW hazards must be stalled instead of eliminated
answers.d: The rename table becomes too large

explanations.d: Rename table doesn’t exist without renaming.
